source.diagram: CaO-SiO2 phase diagram after Muan, Osborn [1], based mainly on the work of Rankin, Wright [2], and with revisions according to Tewhey, Hess [3] and Hageman et al. [4] (miscibility gap), Welch, Gutt [5], Gutt [6] and Gutt, Russell [7] (melting relations involving 3CaO·SiO2) and Trömel et al. [8] (CaO excess in 2CaO·SiO2)
source.caption: Atlas text (printed p. 63): 'Fig. 3.70. CaO-SiO2 phase diagram after Muan, Osborn [1], based mainly on the work of Rankin, Wright [2], and with revisions according to Tewhey, Hess [3] and Hageman et al. [4] (miscibility gap), Welch, Gutt [5], Gutt [6] and Gutt, Russell [7] (melting relations involving 3CaO·SiO2) and Trömel et al. [8] (CaO excess in 2CaO·SiO2). An alternative version of the system in the CaO-rich region, with the stability range of 3CaO·SiO2 between 1300 and 1800 °C, was reported by Trömel et al. [8]. For the polymorphism in 2CaO·SiO2, see also Foster [9] and Hanic et al. [10]. For thermodynamic assessments of the system and calculated phase diagrams, see an Mey [11], Taylor, Dinsdale [12], Eriksson et al. [13] and Hillert et al. [14, 15] (Figs. 3.I to 3.IV).' References: [1] A. Muan, E. F. Osborn: Phase Equilibria Among Oxides in Steelmaking, Ed.: Addison-Wesley Publishing Company, Inc., Reading Massachusetts, (1965); [2] G. A. Rankin, F. E. Wright: Am. J. Sci., 4th Ser. 39 (1915), p. 1/79; [3] J. D. Tewhey, P. C. Hess: Phys. Chem. Glasses 20 (1979) No. 3, p. 41/53; [4] V. B. M. Hageman, G. J. K. Van den Berg, H. J. Janssen, H. A. J. Oonk: Phys. Chem. Glasses 27 (1986) No. 2, p. 100/6; [5] J. H. Welch, W. Gutt: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 42 (1959) No. 1, p. 11/5; [6] W. Gutt: Building Research Current Papers, CP90/68 (1968), 22 p.; [7] W. Gutt, A. D. Russell: J. Mater. Sci. 12 (1977) No. 9, p. 1869/78; [8] G. Trömel, W. Fix, R. Heinke: Tonind.-Ztg. 93 (1969) No. 1, p. 1/8; [9] W. R. Foster: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 51 (1968) No. 6, p. 353/4; [10] F. Hanic, I. Kaprálik, V. Figus, J. Stracelský: Trans. J. Br. Ceram. Soc. 82 (1983), p. 205/7; [11] S. an Mey: PhD Thesis, RWTH Aachen, Germany, (1988), p. 118; [12] J. R. Taylor, A. T. Dinsdale: CALPHAD 14 (1990) No. 1, p. 71/88; [13] G. Eriksson, P. Wu, A. D. Pelton: Canad. Metall. Q. 33 (1994) 13/21; [14] M. Hillert, B. Sundman, X. Wang: Metall. Trans. B 21B (1990) No. 2, p. 303/12; [15] M. Hillert, B. Sundman, X. Wang, T. Barry: CALPHAD 15 (1991) No. 1, p. 53/58.

invariants.notes: Lime + liquid → 3CaO·SiO2. The line runs from the CaO axis to the 3CaO·SiO2 line; the dashed lime liquidus meets it there. Liquid composition not printed.
Solid phases: 3CaO·SiO2 and α-2CaO·SiO2 with CaO in solid solution (Trömel et al. [8]). Liquid composition not printed.

Incongruent melting of 3CaO·2SiO2: α-2CaO·SiO2 + liquid → 3CaO·2SiO2. Drawn 4 °C (≈2 px) above the 1460 eutectic line; the line detector does not separate the two lines (both read 1462.5 °C). Liquid composition not printed; the 2CaO·SiO2 and CaO·SiO2 liquidus curves meet the lines 0.6 wt% apart.
Congruent; field labelled CaO·SiO2 (pseudowollastonite at the melting point).
Silica is tridymite (between the 1470 and 870 °C lines). Composition printed as '(63)'.
Liquid → cristobalite + SiO2-rich liquid. Miscibility gap after Tewhey, Hess [3] and Hageman et al. [4]. Compositions not printed.

liquidImmiscibility.criticalPointNotes: Miscibility gap after Tewhey, Hess [3] and Hageman et al. [4] (caption).
liquidImmiscibility.notes: No crystals inside the dome; it does not change the liquidus (cristobalite disappears at 1695 °C across the gap). Not modelled.

endMemberSources.notes: Not printed in Fig. 3.70: the dashed lime liquidus leaves the frame at the 2600 °C edge near 1 wt% SiO2 (traced axis intercept 2603 °C). The liquidus point at 0 wt% uses the Fig. 3.66 value.
